The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(N=2100\). For a prime \(p\), let \(v_p(n)\) be the exponent of \(p\) in \(n\).

A move replaces a pair \((a,b)\) by \((\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b))\). For each prime \(p\), this replaces the exponents \((v_p(a),v_p(b))\) by \((\min(v_p(a),v_p(b)),\max(v_p(a),v_p(b)))\). Thus for every prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-adic exponents on the board is invariant.

When Mark stops, every possible move is a no-op, so every two numbers on the board must be comparable by divisibility. Sort the final numbers as
\[
x_1\le x_2\le \cdots \le x_{2100}.
\]
Then \(x_i\mid x_j\) for \(i<j\), so for each prime \(p\), the sequence
\[
v_p(x_1),v_p(x_2),\dots,v_p(x_{2100})
\]
is nondecreasing. Since its multiset is the initial multiset of exponents among \(1,2,\dots,2100\), \(v_p(x_k)\) is the \(k\)-th smallest \(p\)-adic exponent among \(1,2,\dots,2100\).

We need the \(2026\)-th smallest final number. Since there are \(2100\) numbers total, this is the \(75\)-th largest exponent for each prime:
\[
2100-2026+1=75.
\]

For a prime \(p\) and integer \(t\ge 0\), the number of integers \(n\le 2100\) with \(v_p(n)\ge t\) is
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^t}\right\rfloor.
\]
So the desired exponent \(e_p=v_p(x_{2026})\) is
\[
e_p=\max\{t\ge 0:\left\lfloor 2100/p^t\right\rfloor\ge 75\}.
\]
Because \(2100=75\cdot 28\), this is equivalent to
\[
p^t\le 28.
\]

Thus:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
p & e_p \\ \hline
2 & 4 \\
3 & 3 \\
5 & 2 \\
7,11,13,17,19,23 & 1 \\
\text{other primes} & 0
\end{array}
\]

Therefore the \(2026\)-th smallest final number has prime factorization
\[
2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]
The number of its positive divisors is
\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 2^6
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
